device.name: CoolLEDX LED Sign
device.notes:
The most common unbranded BLE LED sign platform: car rear-window, bike, backpack, badge and banner signs sold with no brand name, only a screenshot of the CoolLED1248 app (com.jtkj.led1248, ~350k installs).
GENERATIONS: at least seven hardware generations share the "CoolLED*" advertising name — CoolLED (fixed 48x12), CoolLEDA (fixed 32x16), CoolLEDX (variable, 96x16 typical), CoolLEDS, CoolLEDM, CoolLEDU, CoolLEDUD/iLedBike, CoolLEDMX, CoolLEDUX. Two protocol families: "basic" (CoolLEDX and earlier — mapped below) and "advanced" (CoolLEDM and later — same 0x01/0x03 framing and 0x02 escaping, but nearly all command values differ and the text/image payload encodings are opaque). A client MUST branch on the advertised name.
FRAMING (basic protocol): 0x01 | escape(uint16_be payload_length || payload) | 0x03. Because 0x01 and 0x03 are frame delimiters, each 0x01, 0x02 or 0x03 byte anywhere inside the escaped region is replaced by a 0x02 prefix plus (byte + 4):
  0x01 -> 02 05, 0x02 -> 02 06, 0x03 -> 02 07.
0x00 is NOT escaped — it passes through verbatim (confirmed in the vendor app's encoder, 2026-08 audit; the community driver's "0x00 -> 02 04" was wrong). Escape 0x02 first when transforming a buffer or the newly-inserted escape prefixes get double-escaped. Note the schema's `framing.length_prefix` flag below records the length prefix; the escaping layer has no schema representation and is described here.
GEOMETRY IS ADVERTISED, NOT CONFIGURED: the BLE advertisement's manufacturer data carries [0-5] MAC, [6] height, [7-8] width (uint16 BE), [9] color mode (0=mono, 1=7-color, 2=full RGB), [10] firmware version. Manufacturer data shorter than 11 bytes means the device is not a usable CoolLED*. Clients should render content to the advertised geometry rather than asking the user for a panel size.
ERROR CODES (notify): 0x00 success, 0x01 transmission failed, 0x02 device abnormality, 0x03 data error, 0x04 data length error, 0x05 data ID error, 0x06 data checksum error.
CONFIDENCE: service/characteristic UUIDs, advertisement layout, frame structure, escaping rules and the CoolLEDX command bytes for music/text/image/animation/mode/ speed/brightness/switch are HIGH (independent community driver, built from BLE HCI snoops). A 2026-08 static-analysis audit of the vendor app independently confirms the fff0/fff1 service/characteristic, the framing and escaping above, the 0x0A begin-transfer byte and command bytes 0x01-0x09 including mode values 0x01-0x08, speed and brightness; the same app drives CoolLED, CoolLEDA and CoolLEDS through the same basic-protocol builders as CoolLEDX. App-derived facts are source-confirmed but not hardware-verified. Command bytes marked "unconfirmed" below (0x11 show icon, 0x12 power down, 0x13 button on, 0x15 mirror) are LOW and now weaker: they come from secondary references and appear nowhere in the app's basic-protocol builders. 0x23 initialize is in the same position — a CoolLEDM observation, absent from the basic builders. 0x0C invert, 0x0D clear and 0x1F query were observed on a CoolLEDM, not a CoolLEDX. Note 0x0D also exists on the basic protocol, but as password verify — see verify_password below. The text/image/animation payload bodies are client-rendered bitmaps and are NOT specified here; see the coolledx-driver render module. Source: github.com/UpDryTwist/coolledx-driver (original RE credited to CrimsonClyde).
APP AUDIT (2026-08, static analysis of the vendor app — app-derived, not hardware-verified): CHUNKED TRANSFER: large payloads are split into 128-byte chunks, each sent as its own framed command whose command byte is the data type (0x02 text, 0x03 image, 0x04 animation). Chunk body: 0x00 | total payload length (uint16_be) | chunk index (uint16_be) | chunk length (uint8) | chunk data | XOR checksum of all preceding body bytes. The device ACKs every chunk with a 5-byte notification — byte 0 echoes the data type, bytes 2-3 carry the chunk index (big-endian), byte 4 the status (ERROR CODES above) — and the app sends the next chunk only after a success status. A transfer opens with the 0x0A begin-transfer command. CONNECTION: the app requests MTU 247 and paces writes 15 ms apart. PASSWORD: 0x0D verify / 0x0E set exist on the basic protocol. The app applies them to CoolLEDS always and to CoolLEDX only when a password has been configured, so a stock CoolLEDX stays open; physical proximity remains the only access control. FIRMWARE: the app bundles a CoolLEDU OTA image (assets/coolledu.bin) — advanced family, consistent with the OTA note below.
NEW INFO (2026-07 verification — additions only, no discrepancies found): the CoolLED1248 Android app is actively developed (updated 2026-07-02; developer "yfxiong"), with an iOS twin on the App Store (id 1435796557). The advanced-protocol generations support OTA firmware updates through the app (limited on CoolLEDM, comprehensive on CoolLEDU/UX) — signed blobs flow through the app, so sniffing an update is the way to obtain one. Panel hardware per CrimsonClyde's teardown: HC89F0541 8051 MCU, SM16206S LED drivers, 37 kBaud UART between the BT module and the MCU. The same RE documents an overflow bug: declaring more animation frames than are sent makes the sign display raw flash contents (max ~159 frames, roughly 30 kB) — a potential firmware-extraction primitive.

credentials.notes: Anything within radio range can connect and issue commands. Physical proximity is the only access control.

factory_reset.effect: No credential state to clear. Power-cycling drops the current connection, which is the actual remedy for the common failure mode: the device already being connected to another central.

steps.action: Remove power (or battery) for a few seconds and reapply.
steps.expect: Device advertises again and accepts a new connection.

methods.description: No provisioning step: the device advertises as soon as it is powered on and accepts a connection from any central. There is no account, no network credential exchange and no pairing PIN, so a replacement client only has to scan, connect and write.

steps.action: Power the device and scan for its advertisement.
Connect and run the documented initialization sequence, if the spec defines one.

setup.notes: No provisioning. These signs are sold unbranded and identified only by the CoolLED* advertising name; a client needs the generation, not any credential, so identification does all the work setup would elsewhere.

rejoin.notes: Nothing binds this device to a network or an owner, so switching controllers is just connecting from the new one. If the old client is an Android or iOS phone, remove the device from the OS Bluetooth list as well — a cached bond can keep the phone reconnecting automatically and holding the single available link.

variants.notes: Variable geometry, basic protocol. Fully mapped — the only variant this spec drives.
Original, fixed 48x12, monochrome. Basic protocol confirmed in the vendor app (same builders as CoolLEDX, 2026-08 audit), not verified against hardware. Not discoverable.
Fixed 32x16. Basic protocol confirmed in the vendor app (2026-08 audit), not verified against hardware. Not discoverable.

Basic protocol confirmed in the vendor app (shares the CoolLEDX builders per geometry, 2026-08 audit), not verified against hardware. The app always enforces its optional password on this variant. Not discoverable.
ADVANCED protocol. Command table NOT mapped — the basic-protocol commands in this spec must NOT be sent to it. Not discoverable.
ADVANCED protocol, not mapped. CoolLEDUD / iLedBike is the bike variant. Not discoverable.
ADVANCED protocol, not mapped. Believed to be the commercial signs. Not discoverable.
Extends the advanced protocol, not mapped. Not discoverable.

begin_transfer.description: Begin transfer (0x0A). App-confirmed (2026-08 audit): sent once, with no payload, before a chunked text/image/animation upload.

initialize.description: Initialize with a battery-level byte (0x23). Observed on a CoolLEDM only; appears nowhere in the vendor app's basic-protocol builders (2026-08 audit), so unproven — and now weaker — on CoolLEDX.

invert_display.description: Invert the display. Confirmed on CoolLEDM; unverified on CoolLEDX.

mirror_display.description: UNCONFIRMED (secondary source): mirror or similar (0x15). Not found in the vendor app's basic-protocol builders (2026-08 audit) — likely absent on this family.

power_down.description: UNCONFIRMED (secondary source): power down (0x12). Not found in the vendor app's basic-protocol builders (2026-08 audit) — likely absent on this family.

query_status.description: Query (0x1F). A CoolLEDM replied 01 ff 00 01 00. Purpose not fully established; useful as a liveness/handshake probe.

set_animation.description: Set a multi-frame animation. Payload is client-rendered frames.

set_image.description: Set a still image. Payload is a client-rendered bitmap sized to the advertised geometry.

set_mode.description: Set display mode. App-confirmed (2026-08 audit): the vendor app sends 0x01-0x08 (static, left, right, up, down, snowflake, picture, laser).

set_music_bars.description: CoolLEDX: music visualizer, 8 bar heights followed by 8 bar colors (16 payload bytes after the command byte). CoolLEDM sends 8 bytes total.

set_text.description: Set text. Payload is a client-rendered text bitmap sized to the advertised geometry.

show_icon.description: UNCONFIRMED (secondary source): show icon (0x11). Not found in the vendor app's basic-protocol builders (2026-08 audit) — likely absent on this family.

verify_password.description: Password verify (0x0D). App-confirmed on the basic protocol (2026-08 audit), not verified against hardware. Payload: one random byte, then each password digit (one nibble per byte) XOR the random byte, then a XOR checksum of the obfuscated digits. Optional on CoolLEDX — the app sends it only when a password is configured (always on CoolLEDS); 0x0E sets the password. Distinct from the 0x0D "clear" observed on CoolLEDM (advanced family).

characteristics.name: Control
characteristics.notes: Every command is wrapped as 0x01 | escape(uint16_be length || payload) | 0x03. The `value`/`template` byte sequences below are the UNWRAPPED payloads: apply the length prefix, escaping and delimiters before writing. Responses arrive as notifications on this same characteristic.
